title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## StageGuard

### The Breakthrough
StageGuard introduces an agentic distillation framework that extracts stage‑transition reasoning from a large teacher VLM into a lightweight student VLM, enabling fast online decisions without cloud latency. The student model predicts sub‑task completions on the BEHAVIOR‑1K benchmark and demonstrates successful closed‑loop runs on real robots, showing higher prediction accuracy than the baseline teacher.

### The Caveats
The paper reports gains but does not compare StageGuard against any existing stage‑completion baselines, so the improvement magnitude is unclear.

## Workspace Models

### The Breakthrough
Workspace Models create a compact "workspace token" by distilling VLM‑identified salient information during training, allowing policies to query this token at deployment instead of running expensive VLM inference. The token improves manipulation performance on both simulation and real hardware while keeping runtime overhead minimal.

### The Caveats
The paper reports performance gains without naming concrete baseline methods for comparison, leaving the true advantage uncertain.

## FAMOS

### The Breakthrough
FAMOS uses a Multi‑state Articulation Transformer that alternates state‑wise and global attention to fuse sparse, unordered point clouds from multiple monocular views, handling variable numbers of inputs—even a single view—to predict part segmentation and joint parameters. A procedural generator supplies self‑annotated articulated objects for diverse training data.

### The Caveats
The reported gains are unconvincing because the paper does not name any specific feed‑forward or optimization baselines it is compared against.

## Copper‑rs Live Telemetry

### The Breakthrough
Copper‑rs v1.2 streams deterministic "copperlists" with forward error correction, enabling a remote twin to reconstruct missed packets and reorder streams despite loss; recovery points let the twin jump‑start from any consistent state, and log size is reduced by 52.31% while providing on‑the‑fly depth from stereo images.

### The Caveats
The claim of real‑time, loss‑tolerant state cloning is unsubstantiated, as the system is only demonstrated in a simulated packet‑loss demo with no hardware validation or baseline comparison.

## SafeHarness

### The Breakthrough
SafeHarness adds obstacle‑aware route planning (bounding‑box waypoints with replanning) and obstacle‑aware contact execution (collision‑free contact points), raising task success to 71.9% and collision avoidance to 87.5%, a 6.5% and 27.0% improvement over prior SOTA respectively, and outperforming the same agent without harnesses by 2.3× and 1.5×.

### The Caveats
The reported safety gains are demonstrated only in an unspecified simulated setup with no real‑world robot experiments, so it is unclear whether the harness would prevent collisions on hardware.

## Jev Decision Service

### The Breakthrough
Jev (System One) processes typed robot state in 70–500 ms at $0.042 per million input tokens, yielding an estimated $24.57 per million decisions; it triages three judgments per incident for a simulated 10,000‑robot warehouse fleet, offering sub‑second, low‑cost decision making compared to a 149 M‑parameter ModernBERT run.

### The Caveats
The system is only evaluated on simulated incident templates and never on actual robot hardware or edge NPUs, so its claimed sub‑second, low‑cost performance for a real AMR fleet is unproven.

## Egocentric Gig Data

### The Breakthrough
Companies are collecting up to 60,000 hours of egocentric video per month from gig workers wearing head‑mounted cameras, using this large‑scale footage as a pre‑training source for manipulation policies to capture diverse home environments without expensive robot‑mounted data collection.

### The Caveats
The announced acceleration of robot learning rests on untested egocentric footage, as no real‑world robot experiments or quantitative performance metrics are provided.

## OpenHarness

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness provides an open‑source suite of 45 domain‑specific harnesses that let LLM coding agents drive tasks across CAD, PCB layout, game development, and more, with an optional ESP32‑based hardware device for tactile interaction and persistent sessions.

### The Caveats
The repository provides no formal evaluation or comparative benchmarks, so its claim of end‑to‑end AI‑driven creation remains unverified.

### Priority
StageGuard is the most immediately actionable story because it delivers a concrete, lightweight VLM solution that already works on real robots, offering a clear path to improve hierarchical task execution.

### One action
Read the StageGuard paper and prototype its workspace token‑style VLM distillation in your own hierarchical manipulation pipeline.
